'''Tyrone Wallace Jr''' (born June 10, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player and [[point guard]] who recently completed his college career for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]]. As a junior with Cal in 2014–15, he was named a first-team all-conference selection in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]].

==High school==
Wallace attended [[Bakersfield High School]], where he became his school's all-time scoring leader with 1,767 career points.<ref>http://www.nbadraft.net/players/tyrone-wallace</ref> He was also a two-time Bakersfield Californian Player of the Year, and in his senior season in 2012, he was a Second Team All-[[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] selection.<ref>http://www.calbears.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207769714</ref> He was rated the 13th best point guard in the nation by [[Rivals.com]] and given a 4-star rating.

==College==

Wallace chose to attend the [[University of California, Berkeley]] over several other schools, including [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] rivals [[University of Oregon|Oregon]] and [[Arizona State University|Arizona St]]. Coach [[Mike Montgomery]] made him a starter just 10 games into his freshman year, and Wallace responded, averaging 7.2 points and 4.4 rebounds per game the rest of the season.<ref>http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/62208/tyrone-wallace</ref> The Bears would make the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] that year, upsetting a higher-ranked [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] team before falling in the second round to [[Syracuse Orange basketball|Syracuse]].

Wallace continued to make strides in his sophomore year, as he started every game but one and led the team in steals (44) and 3 pointers (43).<ref>http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/62208/tyrone-wallace</ref> By his junior season, Wallace had become a star, as he averaged 17.1 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 4 assists per game. He was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], and was a finalist for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], given to the nation's top point guard. One of his many highlights included hitting a 3 pointer at the buzzer to give Cal a 70-69 victory over USC.<ref>http://www.calbears.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207769714</ref>

On April 23, 2015, Wallace announced he would forgo the [[NBA Draft]] and return to Cal for his senior season.<ref>http://www.californiagoldenblogs.com/2015/4/23/8477583/tyrone-wallace-california-golden-bears-mens-basketball</ref>

==Personal==
Wallace is the son of Tyrone Wallace Sr. and Michelle Wallace. He has a younger brother, Da’zion Wallace, and younger sister, Diamond Wallace, as well as an older brother, Ryan Carolina.<ref>http://www.calbears.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207769714</ref>
